meta.title: Tax Credit Legislation Watchlist
meta.methodology: Curated federal and state tax-credit policy entries. Legislative status source_url fields point to official federal or state legislative sources; market impact text is directional and should be re-reviewed quarterly.

entries.title: 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act enacted (Public Law 119-101)
entries.pricing_impact: Enacts housing-supply and HUD program reforms: new affordable-housing construction becomes CDBG-eligible (up to 20% of a grantee's allocation, post-enactment funds only) and HOME review is streamlined. It does not enact LIHTC or CRA expansion.
entries.source_note: Public Law 119-101 (H.R. 6644, 119th Congress), the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. The GovInfo Public Law text carries the Office of the Federal Register's note that the Act was presented to the President on Monday, June 29, 2026, was not returned within the time the Constitution prescribes, and became law without his signature on July 11, 2026; its legislative history lists the House's final concurrence on June 23, 2026. Section 204(a) adds 42 U.S.C. 5305(a)(28), the new construction of affordable housing, capped at "20 percent of the amounts allocated to the recipient", and 204(c) applies it "only to amounts appropriated after the date of enactment". Section 501(i) strikes 42 U.S.C. 12748(g), the 24-month HOME commitment deadline; 501(l) adds statutory NEPA exemptions for four HOME activity categories, with any rules HUD determines necessary due within 1 year of enactment. Section 405(a) deems a voucher unit in a section 42 building inspected within the preceding 12 months to meet the voucher inspection requirement, if the public housing agency performed that inspection or can obtain its results. Section 1202: no additional funds authorized. The Act does not amend section 42 of the Internal Revenue Code. Public Law text and the pre-amendment 42 U.S.C. 12748(g) (U.S. Code 2024 edition) re-read on GovInfo 2026-10-11. Federal Register searched 2026-10-11 (terms "ROAD to Housing", "Public Law 119-101", and HUD documents on CDBG or HOME since 2026-07-11) for a HUD rule or notice implementing section 204 or 501; none found.

public_law.became_law: without the President's signature (not returned within the time prescribed by the Constitution)

entries.title: Permanent 12% increase in 9% LIHTC state ceiling
entries.pricing_impact: Expands competitive 9% credit authority beginning in 2026. More credit supply can modestly pressure cents-per-credit pricing lower unless investor demand rises with allocation volume.
entries.source_note: Public Law 119-21 (H.R. 1, approved 2025-07-04), section 70422(a), amends 26 U.S.C. 42(h)(3)(I): it strikes the 2018-2021 years and the 1.125 multiplier and inserts calendar years beginning after December 31, 2025 and 1.12, with no end year. Under section 42(h)(3)(I) the multiplier applies to the per-capita and small-state-minimum amounts in 42(h)(3)(C)(ii), after the cost-of-living increase under 42(h)(3)(H); it does not apply to the carryforward, returned-credit or national-pool parts of the ceiling. Section 70422 is the law's only amendment to section 42 besides the bond-financing test in 70422(b), tracked as obbba-lihtc-bond-25pct-test. Amendment text re-read in the GovInfo Public Law 119-21 text, and the pre-amendment section 42(h)(3)(I) read in the GovInfo U.S. Code 2024 edition, on 2026-10-11; no later amendment found.

ceiling_increase.statute: 26 U.S.C. 42(h)(3)(I), as amended by Public Law 119-21 section 70422(a)
ceiling_increase.applies_to_amounts: the per-capita amount and the small-state minimum in 42(h)(3)(C)(ii), after the cost-of-living increase under 42(h)(3)(H)

ceiling_2026.rule: greater of the per-capita amount multiplied by the State population, or the small-state minimum (42(h)(3)(C)(ii))
ceiling_2026.source: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32, section 4.08 (section 2.05 lists the section 70422(a) amendment)

entries.title: 25% bond-financing test for 4% LIHTC buildings
entries.pricing_impact: Adds a 25% route to the 50% bond-financing test for buildings placed in service in taxable years beginning after 2025, if one or more bonds from post-2025 issues together finance at least 5% of basis. Widens 4% eligibility; added bond-credit supply may be priced selectively.
entries.source_note: Public Law 119-21 (H.R. 1, approved 2025-07-04), section 70422(b), strikes 26 U.S.C. 42(h)(4)(B) and inserts a new subparagraph (B): the 42(h)(1) allocation requirement does not apply to a building if (i) 50 percent or more of the aggregate basis of the building and its land is financed by obligations described in 42(h)(4)(A), or (ii) 25 percent or more is so financed and one or more of those obligations are part of an issue dated after December 31, 2025 and finance not less than 5 percent of that basis. Section 70422(b)(2)(A) applies the amendment to buildings placed in service in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025; 70422(b)(2)(B) treats an existing building and a rehabilitation treated as a separate new building under 42(e) as placed in service on the date the expenditures are. No end year. The pre-amendment 42(h)(4)(B) was the 50 percent test alone. Section 70422 is the law's only amendment to section 42 besides the ceiling increase in 70422(a), tracked as obbba-lihtc-ceiling-12pct. Amendment text re-read in the GovInfo Public Law 119-21 text, and the pre-amendment section 42(h)(4) read in the GovInfo U.S. Code 2024 edition, on 2026-10-11; no later amendment found.

bond_test.statute: 26 U.S.C. 42(h)(4)(B), as amended by Public Law 119-21 section 70422(b)
bond_test.bonds: obligations described in 42(h)(4)(A): tax-exempt under section 103 and taken into account under the section 146 volume cap
bond_test.basis: aggregate basis of the building and the land on which the building is located
bond_test.post_2025_min_pct_counted: in aggregate: one or more obligations from post-2025 issues together (42(h)(4)(B)(ii)(II): "1 or more of such obligations")
bond_test.rehabilitation_rule: section 70422(b)(2)(B): an existing building and rehabilitation expenditures treated as a separate new building under 42(e) are both treated as placed in service on the date the expenditures are placed in service under 42(e)(4)

entries.title: Permanent 100% bonus depreciation under Section 168(k)
entries.pricing_impact: Restores permanent 100% additional first-year depreciation for qualified property acquired after January 19, 2025. Treat the Section 168(k) change as an after-tax yield tailwind, not a continuing phase-down headwind.
entries.source_note: Public Law 119-21, section 70301, 100 percent expensing; amendments generally apply to property acquired after January 19, 2025. Section text re-read in the GovInfo Public Law 119-21 text on 2026-10-10; no later amendment found.

entries.title: Permanent extension of the New Markets Tax Credit
entries.pricing_impact: Removes recurring extender risk for NMTC allocation planning after 2025. Pricing still depends on allocation competition, leverage structure, and investor appetite rather than statutory permanence alone.
entries.source_note: Public Law 119-21, section 70423, permanent extension of New Markets Tax Credit. Section text re-read in the GovInfo Public Law 119-21 text on 2026-10-10; no later amendment found.

entries.title: Permanent renewal and enhancement of Opportunity Zones
entries.pricing_impact: Makes OZ rounds permanent (first decennial determination date 2026-07-01); rural QROF investments get a 30% five-year basis step-up. Colorado's new tracts are nominated but not yet certified by Treasury; new zones take effect 2027-01-01.
entries.source_note: Public Law 119-21, section 70421, permanent renewal and enhancement of Opportunity Zones (section text re-read 2026-10-10). Colorado nomination count and date as reported by Government Market News on 2026-10-01; OEDIT's page refused automated access on 2026-10-10, and no Treasury certification of the new round was found that day.

entries.title: Termination of 25C and 25D household clean-energy credits
entries.pricing_impact: Ends two consumer-side home energy credits after 2025, which can reduce after-tax support for owner-occupied retrofit and clean-energy upgrades. Treat homebuyer affordability or rehab assumptions after 2025 as requiring other subsidy sources.
entries.source_note: Public Law 119-21, sections 70505 and 70506, termination of energy efficient home improvement and residential clean energy credits. Section text re-read in the GovInfo Public Law 119-21 text on 2026-10-10; no later amendment found.

entries.title: 45Y and 48E wind/solar credit termination deadlines
entries.pricing_impact: Wind and solar must begin construction by 2026-07-04 or be placed in service by 2027-12-31. A federal court vacated IRS Notice 2025-42 on 2026-06-06, restoring the earlier start-of-construction rules for now. Discount transfers where timing risk is real.
entries.source_note: Public Law 119-21 sections 70512 and 70513 (section text re-read 2026-10-10). Oregon Environmental Council v. IRS, No. 25-cv-4400 (D.D.C.), vacated Notice 2025-42 on 2026-06-06, as reported by Steptoe, Holland & Knight, KPMG and EY; the court docket itself was not read, and no replacement IRS notice was found on 2026-10-10.

entries.title: CRA rulemaking: 2025 rescission proposal and 2026 OCC/FDIC proposed rule
entries.pricing_impact: No final CRA rule. On 2026-08-12 the OCC and FDIC dropped the July 2025 rescission proposal and proposed new CRA rules (comments closed 2026-10-13); the Federal Reserve did not join. Treat bank demand for LIHTC, NMTC and HTC investments as policy-sensitive until a rule is final.
entries.source_note: Federal Register proposed rules: Community Reinvestment Act Regulations, 2025-07-18 (doc 2025-13559) and OCC/FDIC 2026-08-12 (91 FR 52114, doc 2026-16454, comments close 2026-10-13). Federal Register searched 2026-10-10: no final CRA rule since 2025-07-01.

entries.title: Section 6418 transferability for eligible clean-energy credits
entries.pricing_impact: Allows eligible taxpayers to sell all or part of qualifying clean-energy credits for cash. Pricing is negotiated between buyer and seller and generally reflects credit type, tax year, seller credit quality, indemnity, insurance, and recapture risk.
entries.source_note: IRS elective pay and transferability guidance (page reachable 2026-10-10). Section 6418 itself was not amended by Public Law 119-21; the credits eligible for transfer follow each credit's own termination dates.

entries.title: Colorado local-government ROFR/ROFO for multifamily affordable housing
entries.pricing_impact: Creates local-government ROFR/ROFO rights for qualifying multifamily properties; the rights terminate on 2029-12-31 unless exercised before then. Investors should diligence exit timing, notices, and assignment rights in Colorado preservation and Year-15 transactions.
entries.source_note: Colorado General Assembly HB24-1175 bill page and the signed act as published in the 2024 session laws (chapter 286), both re-read 2026-10-11. The act adds part 12 to article 4 of title 29, C.R.S. (29-4-1201 to 29-4-1208), approved 2024-05-30, effective 2024-08-07 (the day after the 90-day referendum period). 29-4-1202: right of first refusal with a matched offer on multifamily or mixed-use rental property of not less than five units that is existing affordable housing (excluding mobile home parks). 29-4-1203: right of first offer on such property of not less than 15 and not more than 100 units that is not existing affordable housing. 29-4-1205 exemptions include (1)(f), a seller that has applied for, is in the process of, or has completed a resyndication or recapitalization under a public affordable housing program and gives the local government notice and evidence; the rights apply if that effort fails. 29-4-1206 limits remedies to damages and statutory penalties against the seller. 29-4-1207: both rights "terminate on December 31, 2029", except that a process exercised before then continues until it concludes. 29-4-1208 repeals part 12 effective July 1, 2031. No amending 2025 or 2026 bill was found, though the legislature's search could not confirm that conclusively. HB23-1190 is related prior-session ROFR legislation but was vetoed and did not become law.

act.statute: C.R.S. 29-4-1201 to 29-4-1208 (part 12 of article 4 of title 29)
assignees: a housing authority within the local government's jurisdiction
a regional housing authority serving it
the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority

rofr.property: multifamily residential or mixed-use rental property that is existing affordable housing (subject to a restricted-use covenant or similar recorded affordability agreement), excluding mobile home parks
rofr.expiration_notice_to: the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority and the local government
rofr.triggering_events: the first of: a material departure from the expiration notices indicating intent to sell, a signed letter of intent, option or other conditional agreement with a buyer, listing the property, or a conditional acceptance of an offer
rofr.intent_notice: the local government makes a good-faith effort to tell the seller, as soon as possible and not later than 14 calendar days after receiving the seller's notice, whether it intends to preserve or waive the right; the notice is nonbinding
rofr.close_exception: if the seller has an entirely cash third-party offer, the local government must close within the period in that offer
rofr.change_trigger: the price in the seller's notice is reduced by 5 percent or more, or its terms or conditions materially change; the local government may exercise or re-exercise the right
rofr.extension: any time period in 29-4-1202 may be extended by written agreement between the local government (or its assignee) and the seller

rofo.property: multifamily residential or mixed-use rental property that is not existing affordable housing, excluding mobile home parks
rofo.notice_timing: before the seller enters into an agreement with a licensed broker to solicit purchasers or otherwise lists the property on the multiple listing service

exemptions.resyndication: (1)(f): seller has applied for, is in the process of, or has completed a resyndication or recapitalization under a federal, state or local affordable housing program, and gives the local government notice and demonstrable evidence; if unsuccessful, the rights apply

remedies.limited_to: monetary damages and statutory penalties against the seller

entries.title: Colorado Transit and Housing Investment Zones affordable-housing credit
entries.pricing_impact: State income tax credit for housing in OEDIT-designated transit/housing zones. CHFA may allocate up to $8.33M annually in 2027-2033, claimable for each of six credit years (seven cohorts; $350M total through 2038), to governmental/quasi-governmental owners that may sell credits.

tz_credit_pairing.source: CHFA 2027-28 QAP, Sections 3.L and 3.L.1 Maximum Credit Award (adopted by the CHFA Board September 25, 2026; approved by the Governor October 23, 2026); amounts unchanged from the Third Draft
tz_credit_pairing.note: Standard annual state credit OR TZ credit where eligible, paired if requested; one allowance, not additive. Amounts are annual state credit per project.

if_no_state_gap_funds.section: 3.L.1 (when state gap funds are not available under the 3.B.9 pilot)

entries.source_note: Colorado General Assembly HB26-1065, Transit and Housing Investment Zones (Transit Investment Area Act); signed and effective 2026-05-27 under the act's safety clause (Section 13 of the enrolled act, confirmed by direct read of the Governor-signed text), credit allocated by CHFA 2027-2033, act repealed 2063-12-31. Pairs a state sales-tax-increment financing tool (OEDIT/Economic Development Commission approves max 3 projects/yr, 6 total, up to $75M diverted/yr) with the housing credit. The enacted text and LLS 26-0227 fiscal note contain no rural credit set-aside, bonus, or enhanced credit (confirmed by full-text search of all 15 fiscal-note pages); statewide geographic equity is instead a criterion for prioritizing otherwise-qualified transit investment projects. Zone eligibility for both the credit and the TIF is gated on OEDIT's Transit and Housing Investment Zone map (due 2026-10-30 per 24-48.5-136), a 2-mile radius around OEDIT-identified transportation facilities; no zone is designated yet, so no development is currently eligible for either mechanism regardless of transit proximity. CHFA's 2027-2028 QAP Third Draft (not yet adopted; it calls this the Transit Zone (TZ) credit and does not name HB26-1065) allocates TZ credit under a separate TZ Credit Allocation Plan, in lieu of standard state credit (p. 17), within the same fixed state-credit amounts paired with 9% and Round Two awards (pp. 31-32), with no TZ-specific scoring points (the only transit points are the TOC/TOD site criterion, which the draft raises from 3 to 5 points and extends to TOC sites, p. 45); monitor draft-to-final for changes before relying on these terms.

entries.title: Neighborhood Homes Investment Act
entries.pricing_impact: Would create a neighborhood homes tax credit for qualifying owner-occupied development and rehab if enacted. Do not size homebuyer subsidy from this proposal until statutory terms and allocation mechanics are enacted.
entries.source_note: 119th Congress House and Senate Neighborhood Homes Investment Act bill pages. Status read from GovTrack on 2026-10-10: H.R. 2854 (introduced 2025-04-10, 70 cosponsors) and S. 1686 (introduced 2025-05-08, 9 cosponsors) are both still at "introduced".

entries.title: Colorado IRA Home Energy Rebates availability watch
entries.pricing_impact: Colorado's HEAR single-family rebates are closed in both regions. Small multifamily HEAR and HER rebates are announced for 2026 but not open. Do not budget a rebate until a program is open.
entries.source_note: Colorado Energy Office home energy rebates page, re-read 2026-10-10: "Important Program Update (Updated August 2026) The HEAR Single-Family Program for Region 1 and Region 2 is closed." and "Rebates for small multifamily buildings will be available in 2026." No launch date is given.

entries.title: Colorado Solar for All / GGRF rescission watch
entries.pricing_impact: Do not count Solar for All as available funding. Colorado's program is on hold after EPA's August 2025 termination; federal courts ruled against the termination in September 2026, EPA may appeal, and Colorado still lists the program as on hold.
entries.source_note: Colorado Energy Office COS4A page re-read 2026-10-10: "The Colorado Solar for All (COS4A) Program is temporarily on hold due to recent developments at the federal level." Court rulings as reported by Smart Cities Dive (2026-09-21) and Utility Dive (2026-10-01); whether they cover Colorado's grant was not confirmed.
